Hi Sara — thanks for the clear example and the sample invoice. Short answer up front: we apply minimums at the billing-unit granularity of the serving instance (model/variant + compute SKU) for each discrete request, but we also have amortization rules that can credit common prefixes/KV reuse across the same conversation id so you usually don’t see two full minimums for a short escalation. Long answer below and a worked matrix attached.

1) Minimums and conversation boundaries
- Minimums (microfloors) are assessed per request onto the serving SKU that handled that request. If a user performs two distinct requests that hit different SKUs (cheaper 8k then 32k), each request is eligible for the microfloor on its SKU.
- However, if the 2nd request is a brief escalation where a significant portion of tokens are covered by KV/prefix reuse, we apply a prefix-crediting rule that reduces effective billable tokens on the expensive SKU. That credit shows as a reduction on the invoice line for the 32k SKU.

2) KV/prefix reuse and crediting
- We track prefix reuse tied to conversation_id. When the 32k invocation reuses cached KV from the 8k invocation, we calculate billable tokens = max(0, invocation_tokens - credited_prefix_tokens). If credited_prefix_tokens cover the majority of the context, the expensive SKU only pays for incremental tokens.

3) Rounding & partial tokens
- We meter tokens at the normalized token unit and round up to the billing quantum (currently 1 token). For microfloors we have a per-invocation floor (e.g., 10 token-equivalent floor) which is then eligible for crediting when amortization applies. So very short escalations can still hit the minimum but could be netted by prefix credits if they exist.

4) Example (attached amort_matrix_v1.xlsx)
- Row examples show: start on model-A (8k), escalate to model-B (32k) with X tokens reused -> invoice line shows microfloor on model-B but line-level credit for prefix reuse reduces net.

If helpful, I can loop in Pricing/Infra to confirm treatment for your specific setup (multi-tenant vs dedicated) and whether we should include a one-off pilot smoothing credit.

Hi all — reviewed with Billing & Serving infra. Confirmations and proposal below.

Confirmed behavior:
- Microfloors are assessed per request on the serving SKU.
- Prefix/KV crediting is applied at line-item level and reduces the net charge on the higher-cost SKU when conversation_id ties the requests.
- Rounding: we report billable tokens rounded up to the nearest token; microfloor thresholds are considered before prefix credits are applied in line-item visibility but netted on the invoice.

Operational note:
- For multi-tenant hosted customers, prefix credits require consistent conversation_id routing; if ClearMart uses different session ids across switches, crediting may not apply. We can instrument a small check during onboarding.

Pilot concession proposal (engineer + commercial):
- Temporary concession for the pilot: waive the 32k SKU microfloor where BOTH conditions hold: (1) net invocation tokens < 60 after tokenization, AND (2) credited_prefix_tokens >= 30. This prevents short escalations with substantial prefix reuse from hitting a 2x-floor.
- Pilot period: 2 billing cycles.
- Additional: Redwood will issue a one-time invoice credit of $2,000 towards the first pilot invoice if you sign by 2028-05-01.

2) Tessa — I can run a quick sample invoice transformation and attach a one-line mock showing the prefix credit (CSV) for Sara.
